unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10-LEVEL: B1.2 THEME 3: PERSONAL LIFE & WELL-BEING

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students create a project titled ''Personal Life and Well-Being'' focusing on the body parts, human illnesses and diseases; human nature and well-being today and in the future; and fashion and personal preferences. Students begin by exploring the human body and describing key body parts and their functions. They then discuss common illnesses and diseases, including ways to stay healthy and prevent these conditions according to their ages and levels. Then, students reflect on human well-being, comparing how people maintain physical and mental health today versus what it might look like in the future. Finally, students explore the role of fashion in personal identity by describing their fashion preferences and how clothing choices affect confidence and self-expression. The project can include written descriptions, illustrations, or creative presentations, such as posters or digital slideshows. Students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''personal life and well-being with its components such as body parts, human illnesses and diseases; human nature and human well-being today and in the future; fashion and personal fashion preferences'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 10 may know what personal life and well-being, human nature, illnesses and diseases mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 10, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''personal life and well-being'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a leg, trousers, cold, flu, to wear'' and also some structures such as ''What’s the matter with you? How are you feeling now? Do you have the flu? Is it boring to live without a smartphone?'' in English from the previous themes or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''personal life and well-being with its components such as body parts, human illnesses and diseases; human nature and human well-being today and in the future; fashion and personal fashion preferences'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a short video clip could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the video clip in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about human nature and human well-being today and in the future; fashion and personal fashion preferences in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Future Well-being Plan Students individually create a future lifestyle plan that focuses on personal health, fashion preferences, and sustainability, including details about diet, exercise, digital habits, and fashion choices. For example, a student might write, ''In 2030, I will exercise five times a week to stay healthy and choose sustainable, cotton-based clothing to protect the environment''. After preparing their plans, students present them in small groups, comparing their ideas using sentences such as, ''This plan is more suitable (sustainable) than my current lifestyle'', or ''It will be as trendy as fast fashion but more eco-friendly''. In the end, the teacher gives feedback on pronunciation, the use of target vocabulary, and target grammar. The students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about human illnesses, diseases and give advice in English through a role play activity by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Doctor & Patient Role-Play Students work in pairs with predetermined roles: Student A as the ''Doctor'' and Student B as the ''Patient''. The teacher prepares papers with symptoms and related advice (e.g., ''headache—take a painkiller'') and places them in a box. Each pair selects a paper. The ''Patient'' uses the symptom to explain their problem (e.g., ''I have a headache''), and the ''Doctor'' gives advice based on the paper (e.g., ''You should take a painkiller''). After each pair performs, the teacher and other students provide constructive and supportive feedback on pronunciation and sentence accuracy. The students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
